zeroModel.name: ClosedNormApplication
sufficientWhen: norm predicate and scope are sufficiently closed for the case
priority/exception structure is already resolved in current effective rules
no materially relevant interpretive choice remains
no prior-case or convention relation changes the result independently

termSeparations.workingTarget: authoritative norm/constraint represented with relatively determinate condition/consequence structure at the queried scope
norm whose application intentionally or practically leaves more case-sensitive classification/evaluation to an authorized process
goal/value/purpose/spirit consideration that can constrain or guide norm application if admitted by current practice authority
condition/argument/norm relation that blocks, narrows or defeats an otherwise applicable default conclusion
two or more current candidate norm consequences cannot jointly determine the same case without priority, scope, exception or other resolution
prior determination/case whose treatment is admitted as a warrant, constraint, analogy or interpretive input for a later case
social/practice regularity or recognized interpretive commitment that may become constitutive when current authority/recognition makes it affect Game semantics
authorized residual choice among more than one materially distinct determination/application compatible with the current norm/application constraints
derived condition where current representation/norm basis does not uniquely settle a materially relevant classification without additional case-sensitive determination or authoritative commitment
current provenance-bound adopted mapping/constraint/stance that resolves or narrows how a norm/term/standard applies in a case class

derived structured subview of AdjudicationCaseContract exposing materially relevant norm sources, scope/currentness, priorities/exceptions, adopted interpretive commitments/precedential inputs and discretion bounds
change in adopted meaning/application mapping while some rule representation may remain fixed
authorized change to current norm/rule content or effective norm relation
temporal scope of which cases/histories/pending determinations a norm or interpretive commitment is authorized to govern

strongLaws: Rule vs Standard is not a universal ontological binary
OpenTexture is a derived relation among representation, case distribution, norm basis and adjudicative closure
NormConflict != requirement for one universal resolution logic
InterpretiveChange can change EffectiveRuleTopology when current authority adopts it and Game semantics change

boundaryCases.case: closed digital predicate
boundaryCases.pressure: zero model succeeds; no explicit open-texture or discretion object needed

boundaryCases.case: same rule text, explicit exception toggled by case fact
boundaryCases.pressure: exception can be represented as current condition/priority relation; no Exception primitive

boundaryCases.case: same default norm, later defeating fact
boundaryCases.pressure: defeasible conclusion changes while norm representation remains; current case basis + applicability relation suffice

boundaryCases.case: two applicable norms with explicit priority
boundaryCases.pressure: conflict resolves through current priority relation, not generic scalar authority

boundaryCases.case: same norms, priority relation changes by authorized policy
boundaryCases.pressure: practical result changes due to effective norm topology/currentness change

boundaryCases.case: IFAB factual vs subjective review categories
boundaryCases.pressure: some predicates are treated as fact-like while others require evaluative/subjective application; no universal rule/standard binary

boundaryCases.case: IFAB Laws + spirit of game + referee discretion within Laws
boundaryCases.pressure: purpose/ethos can be admitted norm-application input but is bounded by the framework, not an unrestricted override

boundaryCases.case: same IFAB text, different case context/intensity classification
boundaryCases.pressure: standard-like term application can leave residual authorized judgment

boundaryCases.case: Magic Comprehensive Rules corner-case reference
boundaryCases.pressure: very detailed rule systems can reduce open cases without eliminating need for specific rulings/procedures

boundaryCases.case: Magic historical 'reasonable pace' standard
boundaryCases.pressure: a norm can intentionally use evaluative language rather than a closed numerical threshold

boundaryCases.case: Magic current rules update supersedes old release-note clarification
boundaryCases.pressure: interpretive/ruling artifacts can become outdated; currentness/source must be preserved

boundaryCases.case: prior judge ruling consulted in later similar case
boundaryCases.pressure: prior decision can be persuasive/relevant without automatically being binding precedent

boundaryCases.case: practice explicitly declares prior ruling/category clarification binding
boundaryCases.pressure: precedent becomes part of current norm basis only through authority/recognition relation

boundaryCases.case: speedrun glitchless category wording fixed, community vote changes allowed technique list
boundaryCases.pressure: same broad term can acquire new adopted interpretive commitment/effective rule topology

boundaryCases.case: speedrun same technique under two category conventions
boundaryCases.pressure: mechanical history fixed while category determination changes with practice norm source

boundaryCases.case: TTRPG novel action with no exact written rule
boundaryCases.pressure: authorized facilitator can select analogy/check/consequence without thereby gaining unrestricted rule-change authority

boundaryCases.case: TTRPG repeated house ruling becomes standing table practice
boundaryCases.pressure: one-off adjudication can become future constitutive norm only if practice adopts/maintains it

boundaryCases.case: judged performance standard with range of permissible scores
boundaryCases.pressure: discretion can be bounded selection among norm-compatible outcomes, not arbitrary freedom

boundaryCases.case: same performance, criteria code/version changes prospectively
boundaryCases.pressure: rule/evaluation change has explicit currentness/version provenance

boundaryCases.case: same performance history reclassified under newly authorized retrospective category interpretation
boundaryCases.pressure: official record may change without rewriting performance history

boundaryCases.case: moderation policy uses context-sensitive harm/harassment standard
boundaryCases.pressure: policy text plus case context can require classification; Game need not own general moral theory

boundaryCases.case: moderation exception for quoted/reporting context
boundaryCases.pressure: exception/defeater can reverse default classification without rewriting the base standard

boundaryCases.case: same text and case basis, two authorized determinations both permitted
boundaryCases.pressure: discretion is residual authorized choice set/region, not lack of norms

boundaryCases.case: same outcome produced once by rule amendment and once by new binding interpretation
boundaryCases.pressure: outcome equivalence does not erase provenance distinction between rule-change and interpretive-change paths

boundaryCases.case: interpretive commitment applies prospectively only
boundaryCases.pressure: new cases change while past certification remains current; temporal scope is independent of content

boundaryCases.case: interpretive commitment applies to pending/historical certification
boundaryCases.pressure: retroactive normative status change does not rewrite underlying event history

boundaryCases.case: case-based reasoning uses prior similar cases as warrants
boundaryCases.pressure: similarity/precedent can supply determination basis without requiring rule closure

boundaryCases.case: two prior cases point in opposite directions
boundaryCases.pressure: precedent set may be conflicting/defeasible; no single precedent primitive or automatic nearest-case rule

boundaryCases.case: Agent proposes literal reading and purpose-sensitive reading
boundaryCases.pressure: both remain candidate interpretations until current adjudicative/interpretive authority adopts one

boundaryCases.case: same Agent holds adjudication but not rule-change authority
boundaryCases.pressure: it may bind case determination without making its interpretation a standing rule for future cases

boundaryCases.case: same Agent is explicitly delegated standing interpretive authority
boundaryCases.pressure: future binding effect arises from delegated scope/currentness, not model identity or language fluency

boundaryCases.case: authorized interpretation changes admissible action set without text edit
boundaryCases.pressure: at GameStructure level this is an EffectiveRuleTopology change even though representation bytes are fixed

boundaryCases.case: community convention is common but officially rejected
boundaryCases.pressure: frequency does not confer constitutive authority; observed practice != current effective norm

boundaryCases.case: rare convention is explicitly adopted by tournament/category authority
boundaryCases.pressure: low frequency can still be constitutive when authority/currentness make it binding

boundaryCases.case: consistency pressure with materially different cases
boundaryCases.pressure: equal treatment requires declared relevance/similarity dimensions; identical outcomes are not always consistency

boundaryCases.case: novel edge case changes which distinctions are relevant
boundaryCases.pressure: case sensitivity can be legitimate without abandoning stable norm sources or provenance

effectiveRuleTopologyAbsorbs: standing interpretive commitment that changes admissible action/evaluation/record semantics
priority/exception relation with current Game-constitutive effect
practice-recognized precedent when given prospective norm force
purpose/spirit clause when current rules make it operative
doesNotAbsorbAsBindingByIdentity: historical ruling with no current precedential force

externalAnchors.source: IFAB Laws 2026/27 Law 5 / Notes / VAR Protocol
externalAnchors.claim: application explicitly combines Laws, spirit of game and referee discretion within the Laws; VAR distinguishes factual and subjective decisions and different review modes
Comprehensive Rules target corner cases; clarifications/rulings are currentness-sensitive and can become outdated when rules update
running-game practice explicitly includes resolving outcomes and improvising answers, a regime where novel cases need not have pre-enumerated closed rules
glitchless categories expose difficult-to-close predicates and community voting/adopted technique lists
nonmonotonic/defeasible normative reasoning demonstrates general mechanisms for attacks, exceptions and norm conflict outside Game ownership
case-based reasoning shows prior cases can act as justification/argument/warrants alongside rules in domains lacking closed causal theories
modern precedential-constraint research formalizes case-based precedent relations, confirming that precedent is a structured reasoning relation rather than raw prior-decision identity

selection.reason: all tested rule/standard/exception/precedent/convention/discretion/open-texture counterfactuals can be represented by GDF0 EffectiveRuleTopology + F3/F4/F5/F6/F8 relations/currentness/authority + GDF3-C AdjudicationCaseContract, provided the contract can expose a NormApplicationBasis subview when those distinctions matter
selection.remainingInternalResidual: No independent norm-application foundation survives; next step should be cross-regime falsification/minimality of the consolidated GDF3 contract before any freeze.
